# pg_procrustes

> A fast, flexible PostgreSQL SQL formatter written in Go. Driven by the native PostgreSQL parser (libpg_query), it understands SQL exactly like the database itself and reformats it according to a declarative YAML configuration.

pg_procrustes reformats PostgreSQL SQL files according to `.pg_procrustes.yaml`. It is idempotent: running it twice produces the same result. It handles plain SQL, DML, DDL, CTEs, and PL/pgSQL function bodies (dollar-quoted blocks). Every option can be set to `preserve`, so the formatter only touches what you ask it to.

For the complete documentation in a single file (README + fully commented reference config), read [llms-full.txt](https://pg_procrustes.80.cz/llms-full.txt).

## Key facts

- Language: Go (CGO, uses libpg_query via pg_query_go)
- License: MIT
- Config file: `.pg_procrustes.yaml` (auto-detected from the directory of each file upward, then from the working directory upward, or `-c <path>`)
- Platforms: macOS (arm64, amd64), Linux (amd64, arm64), Windows (amd64, arm64)
- Install: `brew install heptau/tap/pg-procrustes`, `go install github.com/heptau/pg_procrustes/cmd/pg_procrustes@latest` (then `pg_procrustes --install-templates` for the templates), or a binary from GitHub Releases (the archives include `templates/`)
- Templates: ready-made configs shipped as files (`postgresql` ≈ what PostgreSQL prints, `ai` = lean for LLM prompts, `modern` = lower-case keywords, one item per line with leading commas, friendly to git); a config starts from one with `template: modern` (or a file path, or a list; the file's own settings win)
- Leaving a part alone: everything between `-- pg_procrustes: off` and `-- pg_procrustes: on` (or `/* … */`) is copied to the output untouched
- Editor integration: a built-in Language Server (`pg_procrustes --lsp`: format document / selection, syntax errors as diagnostics) for any editor with an LSP client; Neovim plugin (conform.nvim formatter, `:PgProcrustesFormat`, range formatting), plus config-only setups for Zed, VS Code, JetBrains/DataGrip, Emacs, Helix, Sublime Text, Vim (ALE)

## CLI usage

```
pg_procrustes [flags] [file ...]      # no files → read stdin, write stdout
```

A directory argument is searched recursively for `*.sql` (hidden directories and `node_modules` are skipped); glob patterns work and `**` matches any number of directories (`'migrations/**/*.sql'`, quoted).

- `-w` — write result back to source files
- `--check` — exit 1 if any file would change (CI / pre-commit)
- `--diff` — print unified diff without writing
- `--syntax-errors <fail|skip|ignore>` — what to do with SQL that does not parse (default `fail`: report `file:line:col`, exit 1; `skip` formats the valid statements and leaves the rest as written)
- `--backup[=.ext]` — save original before overwriting (requires `-w`)
- `--out-dir <dir>` — write formatted files to a different directory
- `--lines <a:b>` — format only the statements that touch those lines of a single file or stdin, copy the rest as written (range formatting)
- `--stdin-filepath <path>` — with stdin: the path the text belongs to, so the config is looked up from its directory
- `--lsp` — run as a Language Server over stdio
- `-c <path>` — explicit config file path
- `--print-config` — print the effective configuration (templates resolved, every option) and the files it was built from
- `--list-templates` — list the installed templates
- `--install-templates [--templates-from <url|zip|folder>]` — download the templates of this release from GitHub into the user templates directory
- `-v`, `--version` — print version

## What it formats

- Casing of reserved keywords, keywords, data types, literals, operators, schemas, tables, columns, functions, conditional functions (COALESCE, NULLIF, …), system functions (CURRENT_DATE, …), aliases, PL/pgSQL variables and keywords; per-word casing exceptions
- Data type form: long (`character varying`), short (`varchar`), or long without spaces
- Alias `AS`: add / remove; `<>` vs `!=`; `NOT IN` vs `<> ALL`; `CAST(x AS t)` vs `x::t`; explicit/implicit `ASC`; short/long JOIN form; removing `public.` and safe double quotes
- Spacing: operators, commas, parentheses, inline whitespace; trailing whitespace, trailing newline, semicolons, blank lines
- Layout: clause breaking (including WINDOW), content breaking (comma lists, AND/OR conditions, wrapping of long argument lists and OVER (…) specifications), CASE expressions, subqueries and CTE bodies opened on their own lines (`layout.subquery.break`), `(` placed above its `)` (`layout.paren_indent.open`), UNION blank lines, paren-indented blocks, indentation
- DDL layout (`layout.ddl.*`, all `preserve | never | always | auto`): CREATE TABLE (one column per line, `align`), ALTER TABLE (actions, constraint parts), CREATE FUNCTION / PROCEDURE, INDEX, VIEW, TRIGGER, POLICY, TYPE, SEQUENCE, DOMAIN, EXTENSION, partitions, DROP, GRANT / REVOKE
- PL/pgSQL: DECLARE/BEGIN/EXCEPTION/END structure, IF/ELSIF/ELSE, LOOP/FOR/WHILE, CASE statements, `:=` vs `=` for assignments (`plpgsql_assignment`)

## Top-level config keys

`template`, `reserved_keywords`, `keywords`, `data_types`, `literals`, `operators`, `schemas`, `tables`, `columns`, `functions`, `conditional_functions`, `system_functions`, `aliases`, `plpgsql_variables`, `plpgsql_keywords`, `trailing_whitespace`, `trailing_newline`, `semicolons`, `inequality_op`, `join_form`, `operator_spacing`, `comma_spacing`, `syntax_errors`, `statement_break`, `plpgsql_assignment`, `line_endings`, `comments`, `blank_lines_between_statements`, `arithmetic_spacing`, `blank_lines`, `paren_spacing`, `inline_spacing`, `quoted_identifiers`, `schema_qualification`, `cast_style`, `order_asc`, `not_in`, `layout` (`line_length`, `indent`, `clauses`, `content`, `case`, `union`, `subquery`, `dollar_quote`, `paren_indent`, `ddl`).
